info.title: ATF Extract
info.summary: Document-to-Markdown extraction against the atf-extract contract
info.description:
Converts PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, PNG, JPEG, GIF, TIFF, BMP and WebP into the canonical Markdown defined by `atf-extract/1.1.0`: `## Seite N` page markers, `<figure id bbox page>` entries with normalised geometry, per-page `<summary>` blocks, and HTML tables that preserve merged cells.

Each page is rendered and passed to a vision model together with its text layer. The text layer is authoritative for wording; the rendered page is authoritative for structure.

bearerAuth.description: Static API_TOKEN or an OIDC JWT, depending on AUTHN_MODE. Browser sessions are not API credentials; the UI uses the /ui/* boundary with a cookie.

BoundingBox.description: [x1, y1, x2, y2] normalised to [0,1], origin top-left. Normalised rather than pixels so geometry survives re-rendering the page at a different DPI.

description.description: Self-contained prose; the only retrievable text for the figure.

assetId.description: sha256(reference \n id) — the id Search stores the crop under.

dataBase64.description: Only present when X-Include-Figure-Data is set.

markdown.description: Body only; the page marker is added by the serializer.

sha256.description: Checksum of the uploaded bytes; the only proof two ingests match.

ocr.description: True when at least one page had no text layer, so its text came from the image.

timings.description: Pipeline timings through page assembly; serialization and network delivery are excluded.

timeToFirstPageMs.description: Extraction plus processing of the first page emitted in reading order.

retryable.description: Whether repeating the identical request can succeed.

errorId.description: Correlation id; the full message is in the service log under it.

detail.description: Only present when EXPOSE_ERROR_DETAIL is enabled.

get.description: 503 when the poppler binaries or the vision endpoint are unavailable. Search being unreachable is reported but not fatal, because it only degrades /v1/ingest. `?deep=1` forces a re-probe instead of using the cached result.
Process liveness only — never checks dependencies, so a slow vision endpoint does not cause restart loops. Always 200.
Gates the load balancer on the poppler binaries and the vision endpoint — the same fatal gate as /health, without the LibreOffice and Search reporting. `?deep=1` forces a re-probe.
Includes conversion-specific series: pages, vision requests, token spend, truncations, figure counts and queue depth.

get.summary: Echo the authenticated identity and instance capabilities
get.description: Authenticates with the same chain as every machine route but requires no scope: the answer is the caller's own identity. A client (the Outpost) uses it to validate its configuration before the first upload — a 401 means the credential is rejected, a missing `extract.ingest` scope is a configuration error, and `features.deleteByReference` plus `extract.delete` decide whether mirror-delete can work at all. `limits.maxUploadBytes` is the per-upload ceiling, so an oversized file can be rejected without transferring it.

200.description: The resolved principal and feature/limit advertisement

post.summary: Convert a document to canonical Markdown
post.description:
The response mode is selected by request headers.

- `X-Callback-URL` present: 202 immediately, the result is POSTed to the callback.
- `Accept: text/event-stream`: pages stream in reading order as they complete.
- otherwise: one response at the end, JSON by default, Markdown for `Accept: text/markdown`.

Output conforms to `atf-extract/1.1.0`; see packages/extract-contract.

parameters.name: X-Reference
parameters.description: Stable document identity. Figure asset ids are derived from it. Defaults to the filename for conversion; required for ingest.

parameters.name: X-Title
parameters.description: Overrides the document title. May be `base64:`-encoded.

parameters.name: X-Filename
parameters.description: Filename for the raw-body form, where none is otherwise available.

parameters.name: X-Include-Figure-Data
parameters.description: Embed figure crops as base64 in the JSON response. Off by default: a document with many figures produces a multi-megabyte body.

parameters.name: X-Callback-URL
parameters.description: Switches to asynchronous delivery. Restricted by CALLBACK_ALLOWED_HOSTS; link-local and metadata addresses are always refused. Without an allowlist the host must resolve to public addresses only (private/loopback receivers must be allowlisted); delivery connects to the validated, pinned address.

parameters.name: X-Callback-Events
parameters.description: Set to `extract`, `progress`, or `all` to receive queued, converting, progress, heartbeat and error callback POSTs before the unchanged final callback. Intermediate bodies carry `type`, `jobId` and `job_id`, are serialized per job, best-effort and not retried; they do not block conversion work. One in-flight event and the latest pending event are retained, so slow receivers may miss intermediate progress without creating an unbounded backlog. The terminal completed/failed callback retains CALLBACK_MAX_RETRIES.

requestBody.description: Either multipart/form-data with a `document` field, or the raw file with its own Content-Type. The raw form is intended for service-to-service callers.

schema.description: Ordered accepted, queued, converting, progress, heartbeat, error and done events. Clients must ignore unknown event names for forward compatibility.

post.summary: Convert a document and index it in Search
post.description:
When a database and a Search target are both configured, this route is a wrapper around the v2 job path: the upload is stored in the content-addressed source store, a v2 job is created, and its emitter streams the revision **and figure assets** into Search. A small document is driven inline and answered **200** with the completed result (the historical synchronous shape, now including `job_id` and `revision_id`); a large one is answered **202** with the job id to poll at `/v2/jobs/{id}`. Without a database the route falls back to the original synchronous convert→forward path.

`X-Allowed-Users` and `X-Allowed-Groups` may only *narrow* the caller's own identity; they cannot widen it, unless the caller holds `extract.acl.assign` (or `extract.admin`), in which case the requested lists are applied as sent. The response header `X-ACL-Applied` says which happened.

On the v2 job path every ingest is identified first: a file already indexed in the collection (same bytes, same normalised text, or — for the same reference without file extension — a near-identical text of the same version) is **skipped** and answered `status: skipped` with `duplicate_of`; it is recorded as an additional source of the indexed document. Another format of an indexed document is ingested as a new revision of it (`resolved_reference`), and only a newer version becomes the latest. Without `X-Version` the version is read from the first page (label, then date), else from `X-Source-Modified`. E-mails (`.eml`) are threaded; their attachments are ingested as documents of their own.

parameters.name: X-Reference
parameters.description: Row key in Search. Required, so two uploads named the same do not collide.

parameters.name: X-Title
parameters.description: Overrides the document title. May be `base64:`-encoded.

parameters.name: X-Filename
parameters.description: Filename for the raw-body form, where none is otherwise available.

parameters.name: X-Version
parameters.description: Explicit document version (`2.1`, `Rev. C`, or a date `YYYY-MM-DD`). Skips version detection; orders the document's revisions in Search.

parameters.name: X-Source-Modified
parameters.description: The source file's modification time (RFC 3339 with time zone): the version fallback when the first page states none.

parameters.name: X-Dedup
parameters.description: `auto` (default): skip exact duplicates and same-version near-duplicates of the same document; `exact`: skip only byte/text-identical duplicates; `off`: never skip.

parameters.name: X-Valid-From
parameters.description: RFC 3339 validity start; timezone is required and the value is forwarded to Search.

duplicate_of.description: The indexed source a skipped upload duplicates.

version.description: The version the document was ingested with, and where it came from.

post.summary: Open a resumable upload session, or pull a source_url in one shot
post.description: A JSON body with `source_url` pulls the source in one request (SSRF-guarded by `SOURCE_URL_ALLOWED_HOSTS`; hosts resolving to private, loopback, link-local, ULA, CGNAT or metadata addresses are always refused, the connection is pinned to the validated IP, and redirects are re-validated per hop) and answers **201** `completed`. Any other request opens a resumable session and answers **201** `open` with an `upload_id` and offset 0. A `reference` is required (X-Reference header or `reference` field); the whole-file sha256 may be declared here (`X-Checksum-Sha256`) or at complete time.

parameters.description: Expected whole-file sha256; a bare or `sha256:`-prefixed 64-char hex digest.

size.description: Declared total size; rejected past MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES.

source_url.description: http(s) only; no credentials in the URL.

201.description: Session opened, or source_url pulled and stored.

Location.description: Session URL for a resumable open.

post.description:
Creates a durable job over an already-stored source (referenced by sha256). The job carries a config/pipeline/prompt-hash snapshot, a token budget, and a lease; a worker with a valid lease epoch drives it through `queued → preparing → processing → emitting → committing → completed`, resuming from the first unfinished unit after a crash.

`allowedUsers` / `allowedGroups` set the document's readers, narrowed to the caller's own identity like the `/v1/ingest` headers (a caller holding `extract.acl.assign` or `extract.admin` has them applied as sent; see the `X-ACL-Applied` response header); Search writes them onto every unit and asset check.

`filename` (optional) types the source by its extension; omitted, the reference stands in for it. `collection` must follow Search's naming rule (a letter, then letters, digits or underscores), otherwise the request is a 400.

`pages` (optional) selects one contiguous window of the source in source page numbers: `N`, `A-B`, `A-` (to the end) or `-B` (from page 1). A list such as `1-10,15` or a reversed window is a 400; a start beyond the last page fails the job before any model call; `MAX_PAGES` counts the window. The pages keep their source numbers (contract 2.4: `document.begin.firstPage`). A native source (BPMN, a chart-free XLSX) ignores it.

Optional identity fields: `version` (explicit document version), `sourceModifiedAt` (RFC 3339 file time, the version fallback) and `dedup` (`auto` | `exact` | `off`). A job whose source is already indexed completes without extracting anything; its status carries `duplicateOf`. `resolvedReference` names the indexed document another format was ingested into, `version` the version it was ingested with.

X-ACL-Applied.description: How the requested access list was treated: `assigned` (applied verbatim; the caller holds `extract.acl.assign` or `extract.admin`), `intersected` (narrowed to the caller's identity), `service-empty` (a caller without identity asked for a list; it was discarded and the document is tenant-wide) or `none` (nothing was requested).

get.description: Paginated job overview (`extract.admin`). `order=newest` (default) lists by creation time, newest first. `order=queue` lists the jobs a worker is driving first, then the waiting ones (queued, paused) — both oldest first, the order the queue drains in — then the finished ones, most recently updated first. `status` filters by a comma list of job statuses or the groups `active` and `waiting`; an unknown value is a 400. `total` counts the jobs the filter matches. `include=progress` adds per-stage `progress` and `etaSeconds` to every row (one grouped stage query per page); without it a row carries neither.

get.description: The figure blocks of the job's staged page records in page order (`figureId`, `page`, normalised `bbox`, `kind`, `caption`, `description`, `assetId`), plus the job's `sourceSha256`. Crop bytes are not stored; a client renders them through `POST /v2/render` with the figure's bbox.

post.summary: Render a page or region on demand
post.description: Renders a full page, or a normalised bbox region of it, ON DEMAND from the content-addressed source — full-resolution page images are never pre-stored (Requirement 6.8). Search, which carries no poppler, calls this for zoom / full-resolution and caches the result as an asset variant (Requirement 14.4). The output area is PIXEL-LIMITED (`RENDER_MAX_PIXELS`): a large `targetPixels` or a poster-sized crop has its render resolution clamped DOWN, and the response reports the actual size via `X-Render-Width/Height/Dpi` and `X-Render-Clamped`. The endpoint has its own rate limit (`RENDER_RATE_LIMIT`). Rendering the same `(source, page, bbox, targetPixels)` is deterministic.

delete.description:
Removes the document (all versions of the base reference) from Search. Every non-terminal job of the same reference and collection is cancelled first, so an in-flight emit cannot re-create the document after the delete. The caller's identity is forwarded to Search, which applies the caller's ACL: a caller can only delete documents they could also read.

Idempotent for a client: `200` and `404` both mean the reference is gone afterwards; `404` distinguishes "this collection never held it" (`deleted` would be 0).

post.description:
Removes subject-related data from Extract: jobs (with their staged page, figure, tile, and outbox rows via FK cascade), resumable upload sessions, and content-addressed source blobs that no remaining job references any more. Afterwards the Search cascade runs with the same `requestId`, so a retry stays idempotent on both sides.

Idempotent over `requestId`: a repeat of a committed request replays the stored response; the same id with a different payload is rejected `409`. `dryRun` counts what would be removed and deletes nothing. A store result is honest: `failed` carries the error, `not_configured` marks a target this instance does not have — never a silent success.
